newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary signs contested TV channel franchises.
newsitem.headline: Hungary signs contested TV channel franchises.

text.p: Hungary on Wednesday signed 10-year concessions for two national commercial TV channels with Luxembourg-based CLT's Magyar RTL and Swedish-Hungarian consortium MTM-SBS.
The Hungarian radio and television body ORTT announced on June 30 that the concessions had been awarded to the two groupings.
The CLT-led consortium, Magyar RTL, includes Raiffeisen Unicbank, British group Pearson Plc, publisher of the Financial Times, and Hungarian telecom company Matav.
MTM-SBS is a consortium of the Hungarian-registered company MTM Kommunikacios Rt, TeleMunchen and the majority U.S.-owned company Scandinavian Broadcasting System.
Magyar RTL offered nine billion forints ($47.6 million) for the channel it won, while MTM-SBS offered the set minimum of eight billion forints for the other commercial channel.
Irisz TV, a consortium led by Central European Media Enterprises of the United States, offered 12.5 billion and 12 billion forints, respectively, for the two channels but failed in both bids.
On Monday it said it was challenging the decision and asked a court to forbid signing of the concession contracts.

It said the ORTT had breached regulations when assessing the bids and violated the tender procedures. On Wednesday it announced it had a public document showing that one of the winning tenders was illegal.
After the signing, ORTT Chairman Mihaly Revesz said he had no comment on the statement and added that the case would be settled in court.
"I haven't seen (the statement) and I don't have any comment, especially as this is an ongoing legal process," Revesz told Reuters.

The eight-member ORTT board chose the winning bidders after two rounds of discussion, saying one important factor was the future diversity of Hungary's media scene and that the verdict was unanimous but for one abstention.
The 10-year franchises can be extended by another five years without the need for a second tender. The two television channels will have to start broadcasting on October 7 at the latest.
